agent.problem: Cards 2, 6, 7, 11, 14 and 17 provide no earlier-card basis for reliably distinguishing the right answer from the alternatives. That makes six of the eleven choices dependent on luck or prior Bible knowledge, so discovery questions dominate instead of remaining a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Card 5 does not supply heaven or enough context to infer it rather than Sinai or Carmel. The blank therefore asks for unrevealed wording instead of testing a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Card 16 never mentions Zion or provides a way to distinguish it from Egypt or Babylon. The baker can only guess the unrevealed place name or rely on prior knowledge.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
